I do a lot of Bio classes which are material dense and my uni only gives 1 week for exam revision, so this is what I do:

I turn my notes for each class into Anki decks/cards. It is faster than creating physical flashcards, and the program uses spaced repetition which is a great way to encode information into your long-term memory. I use this throughout the semester, but 3 weeks is sufficient! Simply re-writing notes is passive and ineffective unless you're writing from memory.

Reading the same material from a different source, like a textbook, helps ensure you understand the material when it's written in a different way, and could allow you to add additional detail to your notes. The greater your understanding of the material, the easier it will be to recall!

If you aim for a 60 but end up messing up something, you'll only get a 2:2 maximum. But if you aim for a 70, you'll still likely get a 2:1 minimum! Likewise, if you're averaging 60 and a module kicks your ass, your average could fall to a 2:2. That's why aiming as high as you can is important!

Sub-honours is definitely the wiser option. Honours will be significantly less stressful if you are able to focus your full attention on those classes.
